criteria.reasoning: The memo states the catering contract "Involved an undisclosed Financial Interest and conflict of interest through Director Thomas Aldana, whose spouse, Celeste M. Aldana, is the 100% sole owner and manager of the entity." It treats the contract as a policy violation.

It names both failures: "Thomas Aldana answered 'No' to Question 2 on January 20, 2026, twelve days after Saffron & Sage submitted its bid," and at the February 12 meeting "Director Aldana remained silent ('No other director made a disclosure')."

It cites the recusal requirement (Art. III, Secs. 2, 3(a)) and finds he "Did not recuse; actively participated in discussion, spoke in favor of Saffron & Sage," and "Made the motion ... and voted in favor."

It states that had he recused, "the vote would have stood at 5 in favor and 5 opposed," that "a tie vote fails" under the bylaws, and that "Director Aldana's improper vote directly caused the adoption of the motion."
It states the board bypassed "the Gala Committee recommendation (Harborview Provisions at $52,900) to award Saffron & Sage at $68,400 ($15,500 higher)." Both bids and the difference are correct.

It finds Ramaswamy complied at every step: the annual statement, written disclosure to the Chair, oral disclosure, leaving the room, and approval of the lowest bid of $18,250 "10–0 by remaining disinterested directors." It concludes "The Conflict of Interest Policy was fully satisfied in all respects" and recommends no action regarding her.

It concludes Saffron & Sage is "reportable on Schedule L, Part IV" of the 2025 Form 990 (FY July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026). The reasons given are the 100% spouse ownership ("exceeding 35%") and the $71,860 "exceed[ing] the $39,400 threshold."
It computes "1% of $3,940,000 = $39,400" and "The greater of $10,000 or $39,400 is $39,400."

It states "$18,250 does not exceed the $100,000 threshold or the $39,400 threshold" and "BrightStage is not reportable on Schedule L, Part IV," after treating BrightStage as an interested-person entity through the director's brother.

The memo does include the notice-and-explain step ("must immediately inform Director Aldana in writing ... opportunity to explain ... within 15 days"). But it also states as fact that the board could not make a determination "because Director Aldana concealed the Financial Interest." This asserts deliberate concealment before he has been heard, which the criterion makes a failure.

It requires the contract to "be re-reviewed by the disinterested directors under Article III, Sections 3(c) and 3(d)," including whether a more advantageous transaction was available (citing Harborview's $52,900). It adds that "If the re-review determines that the Theatre paid more than fair market value, the board must consult legal counsel" on IRC 4958 and recovering the excess, without declaring an excess benefit settled.

It notes "Director Aldana is currently a member of the Governance Committee," quotes Article IV, Section 4, and says the Chair and Naomi Sato "must handle this matter without Director Aldana's participation or presence."

It states the board, "Acting by a majority vote of disinterested directors," determines whether he failed to disclose and imposes disciplinary action. It also says "Director Aldana must file a corrected annual conflict-of-interest statement within 30 days of the board's determination."
